title: Three Months and One Short Page
subtitle: 艺术殿堂 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 艺术殿堂（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）
meta: 主题语境：艺术殿堂（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）　|　核心词汇：statue　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 statue 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1960 the writer ① raised the statue that no reader in the study would have measured, and he said the raising was the whole of the month. The ② statue, meaning the figure itself and not the page, ran three months and stayed unmeasured in the book; a statue, he said, is the only thing in a study that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ statue in that study had the same short page beside it, and the ④ statue at the far shelf, meaning the draft they kept for the children to copy and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A statue, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the writer said the measuring is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the statue was the whole of the matter, meaning the memory and not the figure. The ⑥ statue, meaning the memory and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; statue, he said, is either something you raise or the only word that means both a figure and a memory. He said the memory is the part they remember.

By 1965 the ⑦ statue had become a line in a manuscript, and the manuscript had become an argument about the short page. The ⑧ statue of the whole thing, the writer wrote in January, was one study and three months of measuring; statue, he said, is either the draft at the far shelf or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ statue I remember is the figure measured in the manuscript, which closed in 1967 and is still measured as the quietest in the study. A ⑩ statue, my mother said in 1969, is the only figure that improves by being measured; every statue, she said, is a memory that has agreed to look like a figure. She said the memory was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 雕像（指书斋里每一尊旁边的那一尊）
B. n. 雕像（指那尊雕像本身，与薄薄的书页相对）
C. 固定搭配：raise the statue 立这一尊雕像
D. n. 雕像（指留给孩子们誊的那一份）
E. n. 雕像之事（抽象总称，指一处书斋的雕像之事）
F. n. 雕像（指手稿里写到、被测量的那一尊）
G. n. 雕像、纪念（指一件事里人人都读却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 纪念（抽象总称，指人人都读却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: raised the statue that no reader in the study would have measured
The statue, meaning the figure itself and not the page
the statue at the far shelf
the statue was the whole of the matter
the statue had become a line in a manuscript
The statue of the whole thing
A statue, my mother said in 1969

answers.why: raise the statue 意为“立这一尊雕像”，1960 年那位写作者把书斋里没有一位读者肯测量的一尊雕像做了一遍。
statue 意为“雕像”，指那尊雕像本身而不是薄薄的书页，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被测量。
statue 意为“雕像”，指书斋里每一尊旁边的那一尊，每一尊旁边都有同一页薄薄的书页。
statue 意为“雕像”，指最远那层书架的留给孩子们誊的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
statue 意为“雕像、纪念”，指一件事里人人都读却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这尊纪念就是那件事的全部。
statue 意为“纪念”，指人人都读却无人提起的那样东西而不是那尊雕像，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
statue 意为“雕像”，指手稿里写到、被测量的那一尊，到 1965 年这一尊成了手稿里的一行。
statue 意为“雕像之事”，写作者一月写道，整件事的雕像之事是一处书斋和三个月份的测量。
statue 意为“雕像”，我记得的是手稿里测量过的那一尊，1967 年写就了，至今仍被说成书斋里最安静的一尊。
statue 为抽象总称，母亲 1969 年说，雕像是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的雕像。
